# BRAIN ABSCESS WITH TOXOPLASMA GONDII

Prior to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic (CT) - guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess material for determination of infectious pathogen. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy based on pathogen once isolated.

Central nervous system toxoplasmosis occurs mostly in HIV-infected patients.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Continue treatment for a minimum of 6 weeks after resolution of signs/symptoms, followed by suppressive therapy until sustained immune reconstitution occurs.

Suppression can be discontinued if CD4 count >200 for 6 months.

---

References:

- Brouwer et al. N Engl J Med, 2014, 371(5)447-56
- Mandell chapter: Brain Abscess
- Sanford keyword: Brain Abscess, Toxoplasmosis
- Up-to-Date article: Toxoplasmosis
Therapy:
Preferred:

Patient weight >/= 60 kg
Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO x 1 then 75 mg po daily ($$$$$) DI,O <AND>
sulfadiazine 1.5 gm PO q6h ($$) [DI,O] <AND> leucovorin 10 to 25 mg po daily ($)

< OR >
Patient weight < 60 kg
Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO x 1 then 50 mg PO daily ($$$$$) DI,O <AND>
sulfadiazine 1 gm po q6h ($$) [DI,O] <AND> leucovorin 10 to 25 mg po daily ($)

Alternatives:

Patient weight >/= 60 kg
Pyrimethamine 75 mg PO q24h ($$$$$) DI,O <AND> clindamycin 600 mg PO q6h

($) [H,O] <AND> leucovorin 10 to 25 mg po daily ($)

< OR >
Patient weight < 60 kg
Pyrimethamine 50 mg PO q24h ($$$$$) DI,O <AND> clindamycin 600 mg PO q6h

($) [H,O] <AND> leucovorin 10 to 25 mg po daily ($)

< OR >
Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$) R,DI

< OR >
Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg PO q12h ($) R,DI
